rows.statement: The overview resource still presents databaseobject-children, databaseobject-create, and databaseobject-properties-get/set as currently implemented tools.
rows.replacement: Replace with tree-first overview built around databaseobject-tree-get, databaseobject-tree-apply, palette-list, palette-describe, requestable-execute, and the built-in capabilities resource.

rows.statement: The MCP usage guide is centered on removed create, children, and properties-set flows.
rows.replacement: Retire or rewrite around the live tree-first contract and the built-in capabilities and quickstart recipe resources.

rows.statement: The context API guide remains valid because it focuses on Rhino runtime guardrails rather than obsolete MCP tool names.
The JSON quick reference still relies on databaseobject-children and older sequence-building assumptions.
rows.replacement: Keep the step semantics, but rewrite the workflow examples around databaseobject-tree-get, databaseobject-tree-apply, and requestable-execute.

rows.statement: The sequence quickstart depends on removed create, children, and properties-get/set tools.

rows.statement: The transaction quickstart contains useful HTTP guidance but still references create and properties-get flows that are not live anymore.
rows.replacement: Keep the HTTP connector guidance, but rewrite the MCP workflow around tree-apply, tree-get, databaseobject-schema, and requestable-execute.

rows.statement: The UI quickstart is still based on databaseobject-children and databaseobject-create and databaseobject-properties-set.
rows.replacement: Replace with a UI guide built around tree-get, tree-apply, palette-list, palette-describe, mobile-builder-open, and marketplace tools.

rows.statement: The only exposed prompt still instructs agents to use removed create, children, and properties-get/set tools.
rows.replacement: Replace with a canonical start prompt that tells agents to read built-in resources first and then use the live tree-based tool surface.

rows.statement: Several resource descriptions still advertise create, properties-set, and curl-first workflows that are no longer canonical.
rows.replacement: Refresh the descriptions after the guides are rewritten so the list view itself becomes trustworthy onboarding.

rows.statement: The main CLI prompt instructs use of removed related-based create flows and old schema expectations.

rows.statement: Planner plus specialists, dependency order, and acceptance gates are reusable pattern ideas.
